title: Marx: Analysis, Prediction, and Historical Outcomes
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Marx's writings examine capitalism as a historical system rather than a timeless form of exchange. He asked how property, production, wage labor, law, and political power fit together. Historical materialism gives material production and social relations a central explanatory role, but the metaphor of an economic “base” and a cultural or political “superstructure” can mislead if treated as a one-way machine. Institutions and ideas can also stabilize, contest, and reshape economic relations.

Marx distinguished those who control productive assets from workers who must sell their labor power. His account of exploitation links profit to the organization of production and the appropriation of surplus. His concept of alienation asks how workers may lose control over what they make, how they make it, and how they relate to others. These concepts are analytical claims; accepting them requires evidence and argument, not loyalty to a label.

Marx also made historical expectations about class conflict and capitalism's transformation. Some formulations sound strongly directional, but capitalist societies developed in varied ways: labor law, unions, welfare institutions, ownership structures, technology, and global trade altered conflicts without eliminating them. A theory can identify a mechanism without predicting every path or date correctly. Failed inevitability is not the same question as whether a concept remains useful.

Twentieth-century governments that invoked Marx built very different institutions under war, revolution, scarcity, and geopolitical pressure. Many produced coercion and severe restrictions on liberty. These outcomes belong in any evaluation, but intellectual influence is not a simple transfer of a complete blueprint from author to state. Careful judgment asks which texts, interpretations, institutions, and decisions connected an idea to an outcome. It can reject repression while still testing whether class, ownership, alienation, or crisis helps explain contemporary evidence.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every later state followed one complete plan written by Marx.

options.label: B
options.text: Marx's concepts, predictions, and later political outcomes should be evaluated separately but relationally.

options.label: C
options.text: Economic relations are never affected by institutions or ideas.

options.label: D
options.text: A failed prediction makes every analytical concept meaningless.

questions.answer: 正解：B。分析概念、歴史予測、後世の政治的結果を区別しながら媒介関係を検討します。Aは媒介過程、Cは相互作用、Dは予測と概念の別評価を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage warn against treating base and superstructure as a one-way machine?

options.label: A
options.text: Political, legal, and cultural institutions can stabilize, contest, and reshape economic relations as well as be influenced by them.

options.label: B
options.text: Economic and social relations have no explanatory role at all.

options.label: C
options.text: Ideas and institutions are always identical to productive assets.

options.label: D
options.text: The metaphor proves that culture can never affect the economy.

questions.answer: 正解：A。政治・法・文化は経済関係から影響を受けるだけでなく、それを安定化・争点化・再形成し得ます。B～Dは双方向性を消します。

questions.prompt: The word “appropriation” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: taking control or possession

options.label: B
options.text: refusing to produce anything

options.label: C
options.text: measuring public opinion

options.label: D
options.text: predicting an exact date

questions.answer: 正解：A。ここでは生産された剰余を取得・占有することです。B～Dは生産拒否、世論測定、日付予測であり文脈と異なります。

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what forms of control may workers lose through alienation?

options.label: A
options.text: Control over what they make, how they make it, and how they relate to others

options.label: B
options.text: Only control over the weather outside the workplace

options.label: C
options.text: Ownership of every cultural and political institution

options.label: D
options.text: The ability to predict an exact date of historical change

questions.answer: 正解：A。生産物、作業方法、他者との社会的関係への統制喪失を指し、単なる退屈ではありません。B～Dは本文の概念に含まれません。

questions.prompt: Why are the usefulness of an analytical concept and the accuracy of a prediction of historical inevitability separate questions?

options.label: A
options.text: One tests whether all history follows a predicted path, while the other tests how well a concept explains particular evidence or mechanisms.

options.label: B
options.text: A concept is useful only if it predicts every path and date exactly.

options.label: C
options.text: Historical predictions and explanatory concepts always have identical criteria.

options.label: D
options.text: Evidence is unnecessary for evaluating either question.

questions.answer: 正解：A。必然予測は歴史経路の普遍性、概念は特定の証拠・機構への説明力を問うため基準が異なります。B～Dは二つを混同するか証拠を捨てます。

questions.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Capitalist institutions have been identical across all countries and periods.

options.label: B
options.text: Rejecting coercive governments requires rejecting every question about ownership.

options.label: C
options.text: Later outcomes should be traced through interpretations and institutional decisions.

options.label: D
options.text: Marx wrote no claims about historical change.

questions.answer: 正解：C。思想から結果までを文書、解釈、制度、意思決定を通して追う必要があります。Aは制度差、Bは批判と分析の両立、Dは歴史予測の存在を否定します。

questions.prompt: What role do labor law, unions, and welfare institutions play in the argument?

options.label: A
options.text: They show that capitalist societies did not follow one unchanged path and that institutions can alter conflict without necessarily eliminating it.

options.label: B
options.text: They prove that class conflict disappeared everywhere.

options.label: C
options.text: They show that institutions never affect economic relations.

options.label: D
options.text: They confirm every exact prediction of inevitable transformation.

questions.answer: 正解：A。単一の不変経路への反例・条件変更として予測の強さを弱めますが、対立の完全消滅までは証明しません。B～Dは本文より強すぎるか逆です。

questions.prompt: What does “Failed inevitability is not the same question as whether a concept remains useful” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: A historical prediction can fail even when a concept still explains some observed mechanisms or evidence.

options.label: B
options.text: If one prediction fails, every concept must be discarded without testing.

options.label: C
options.text: Concepts are useful only when history has one inevitable path.

options.label: D
options.text: Historical predictions cannot be evaluated with evidence.

questions.answer: 正解：A。前者は必然的歴史予測、後者は個別現象への説明力であり、一方の失敗から他方を自動的に否定できません。B～Dは評価対象を混同します。

questions.prompt: Which evaluation best addresses the claim that oppressive twentieth-century regimes invalidate every Marxian concept?

options.label: A
options.text: Condemn repression and trace texts, interpretations, institutions, leaders, wars, and conditions, while testing each analytical claim separately against evidence.

options.label: B
options.text: Excuse repression because governments used Marx's name.

options.label: C
options.text: Assume citation proves that every state policy followed directly from every concept.

options.label: D
options.text: Ignore political outcomes and accept all concepts without evidence.

questions.answer: 正解：A。抑圧を批判しつつ、思想から政策への媒介過程と各概念の経験的説明力を別々に検証します。Bは免責、Cは直接転写、Dは結果と証拠の無視です。
